newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. rate fears send Euro bourses tumbling.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. rate fears send Euro bourses tumbling.

text.p: Fears of looming higher interest rates sent European bourses scurrying lower after a surprise jump in the core U.S. inflation rate for March.
Investors took fright at the robust inflation data coupled with a large upward revision in February retail sales, which raised the likelihood of further rises in U.S. interest rates.
Wall Street shed more than 75 points after its opening, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to introduce programme trading curbs.

Shares in London reversed their morning gains, with the benchmark FTSE-100 index trading down 0.75 percent. Germany and France turned even more negative, with their main indices losing well over one percent.
Continuing signs of a strong U.S. economy and expectations of higher interest rates helped to underpin the dollar in late European trade, despite a tumble by the U.S bond market.
The dollar hovered just below a three-year high against the German mark and 57-month high versus the yen.
Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International in London, warned the dollar's run could begin to eat into U.S. corporate earnings, which would further erode Wall Street prices.
"If we don't get intervention from the central banks, the dollar is going to keep on rising, which has to have an impact on earnings," he said.
Sterling rode on the dollar's coattails to scale a new 4-1/2 year peak against the mark, extending its assault on a generally feeble German currency.

The pound punched through 2.80 marks for the first time since September 1992, when it was ejected from the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM). But against the dollar, the British currency was stable.
Sterling's gains against the mark had more to do with weakness plaguing the German currency than sterling-specific factors, said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Revived optimism that a broad-based European single currency will get off the ground as scheduled in 1999 helped to drive the mark to new lows against other European units.
German carmaker Volkswagen proved one of the few star performers on Friday, as its shares soared to record highs on an extremely upbeat outlook for 1997 and a series of analysts' buy recommendations.
The company's results got a hefty lift from the mark's decline in currency markets.
Market sentiment on the dollar's strength against the yen remained positive despite confusing comments from Japanese officials overnight about concern over the yen's recent slide.

Cabinet minister Kabun Muto cautioned that an artificial attempt to forestall a further slide by the yen might not be effective. But the Ministry of Finance quickly distanced itself from his comments saying they did not reflect official policy.
The ministry emphasised that the official view was that the yen's recent falls were overdone and the ministry was concerned about it.
Although the United States reported that wholesale prices (PPI) fell for the third month in a row in March, the picture was less benign when the often-volatile food and energy sector was excluded.
This so-called core rate, which economists believe more closely tracks inflation, rose 0.4 percent in the month after falling 0.1 percent in February.

"The (retail sales number) with the revisions is a bit stronger than it looked, and the PPI, if you (exclude) energy is really not particularily good, a little disappointing," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7225 marks and 126.10 yen, compared with 1.7177 and 126.02 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 32.9 points at 4,288.3.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 11.44 points at 3,340.05. The electronic IBIS index fell 1.24 percent, or 41.57 points, to 3,311.01.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 35.18 points lower at 2,572.79.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $347.95 an ounce, compared with the London close of $347.85 on Thursday. Silver was three cents lower at $4.78.
